narrative:
The model estimates a 42% chance that you will not pass your final year. Under the school’s decision rule, that places you in the fail-risk group, so remedial courses are required. This is a warning rather than a certainty: roughly two in five students with a similar profile would not pass.

The strongest reason for the prediction is your history of one past class failure. Students who passed averaged no past failures, so this is the main signal pushing the model toward “will fail.” The next most influential factors actually work in your favour: you come from a small family of three or fewer people, and you report good family relationships. Both are linked with passing and reduce your risk, but they do not outweigh the concern raised by the past failure.

To improve your position, focus on not repeating a failure in your current courses and use available help early. Your weekly study time is under two hours, while most passing students study two to five hours, so building a steadier routine would help. Although you receive family support, you are not taking paid classes or school extra support; asking teachers about structured support and attending consistently would also reduce your risk.
